notes:
Short summary: mid-market product analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood starting with Hosted API for fast integration, moving to Dedicated if POC meets throughput and cost targets. Key ask: embeddings throughput for nightly bulk updates + low-latency semantic search for interactive product analytics UI.

Background & context: Olive Branch InsightWorks provides in-product analytics and contextual help for B2B SaaS customers. They run a nightly indexing pipeline that embeds ~12M docs/month (batch jobs + incremental updates). Current prototype uses open-source models + self-hosted embedding pipelines; they want a managed route to reduce ops burden and improve latency for UI search.

What they care about (direct from AE/PM calls):
- Throughput: need ~400 concurrent embedding requests during nightly jobs (can be run as batched bulk), target wall-clock completion <3 hours for nightly full run.
- Online latency: semantic search API for UI needs 50-120ms p95 for single-vector lookup + reranking stage.
- Vector DB integration: must work with their managed Milvus cluster (or optionally Pinecone). Prefer connector or straightforward export/import (bulk upsert API + incremental upserts).
- Cost: mid-market sensitivity, looking for model × compute sizing to stay in $50k–$150k ARR band for service fees. Interested in suggestions from Redwood Optimize (batching/quant guidance).
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, audit logs for embeds/queries, KMS-backed keys, and EU data residency for customers in EMEA.

Engagement history and current status: see timeline. POC underway using Hosted API (rate-limited keys) for functional proof and throughput benchmarking. Recent benchmark run did 1M embeddings in 2h45m using aggressive batching but observed 18% variance due to cold-starts and transient GPU throttling. SE recommends Dedicated with reserved pools to stabilize throughput.

Quote snippets / paraphrases from contacts:
- "We need predictable nightly windows — variance hurts downstream reporting." — Head of Data (Claire Martinez)
- "If Dedicated locks to a commit we can forecast cost and capacity, that's attractive." — VP Product (Evan Ryder)

Decision criteria (stated):
- POC throughput meets nightly SLA (<3h full run)
- Online search p95 latency within target at 1k QPS simulated traffic
- Clear integration path to Milvus + affordable committed monthly price
- Security checklist passed (SAML, audit logs, KMS)

Recent notes / next actions (short bullets):
- 2026-02-21: Kickoff POC (Fireflies id ff-2026-02-21-olivebranch-kickoff). Hosted API keys provisioned; basic embedding flows tested. Action: Rafael to run throughput matrix.
- 2026-03-01: Benchmark run #1 completed; artifacts in drive (throughput-benchmarks.xlsx). Observed 18% throughput variance. SE note: investigate cold-starts and prefix caching.
- 2026-03-04: Security questionnaire submitted; asked clarifying Qs on audit log retention and KMS BYOK. Drive link: security-faq in shared folder.
- 2026-03-05: Pricing intro call. Finance requested a committed Dedicated SKU estimate and autoscale burst policy costs. AE to prepare 12-month vs 24-month pricing options.
- 2026-03-12: Demo of Dedicated runtime (internal); SE suggested reserved pool for nightly batch + smaller pool for online inference.
- 2026-03-18: Upcoming: Dedicated sizing + procurement stakeholders call. Owner: Jordan. Goal: get procurement requirements and sign off on forecast.

POC technical notes (SE):
- Batch strategy: use large-batch prefix caching + KV reuse. Recommend chunking to 2048 tokens for embeddings job to reduce per-item overhead.
- Vector DB flow: upsert via bulk API; need idempotent ingestion pattern; include checksum metadata to avoid re-embedding unchanged docs.
- Fallbacks: recommend model variants with smaller quantized footprints for cheaper nightly runs; route interactive search to higher-capacity model.

Open issues / blockers:
- Confirm EU data residency approach for multi-tenant Hosted API vs Dedicated VPC regioning.
- Finance pushing back on committed GPU hours pricing — needs clearer unit economics showing net savings vs self-hosting.
- Nightly SLA: define acceptable retry/backoff policy for partial failures during bulk upserts.

Suggested AE playbook items:
- Share Optimize report: expected savings with batching + quantization (customized to their 12M/mo doc volume).
- Run a dedicated-stability POC simulating 3x load to measure p95 variance before commit.
- Provide a Milvus connector implementation note + sample script (upsert idempotency).

Summary: Strong fit for Redwood's mid-market motion. Technical heaviest asks are standard (batch throughput + vector DB integration + residency). Primary friction is cost/commit sizing. If Dedicated POC proves stable throughput and we present a transparent pricing scenario, likely to move to procurement in April 2026.
